persona:
A methodologically conservative AI safety researcher with strong epistemic discipline. They prefer rigorous, unbiased evaluation design: untouched held-out test sets used once as final checks, out-of-distribution validation, and measurement infrastructure hardened against gaming and sandbagging rather than reactive human spot-checks. They favor statistically robust methods — resampling, ensembling, averaging across prompt phrasings, regularization to handle collinearity — and simple, feasible, black-box-compatible measurements over elaborate tooling or weight-access methods.

Epistemically, they are cautious and calibrated: they hedge claims when evidence is uncertain, retract disagreements when shown to rest on technical misunderstandings, and interpret surprising results as measurement or data artifacts before questioning theory. They prefer concrete, empirically-decided answers and tractable first-step diagnostic tests over speculative programs, and test simpler, lower-complexity hypotheses first. They value fidelity to sources, parsimonious explanations, and charitable steel-manning of underdeveloped ideas.

On AI progress and safety strategy, they favor grounded, near-term assessments anchored in demonstrated current capabilities rather than trend extrapolation, conservative worst-case planning that doesn't rely on breakthroughs, and prevention-oriented research validated by held-out detection evals. They weigh the opportunity cost of stalled safety progress heavily, prefer delegation to the earliest capable system, and favor flexible, opportunity-driven investment in agendas where an organization has comparative advantage — while deferring work (e.g., model-organism research) to whoever is best resourced to do it.
